questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Battle of Porto Novo (1781):
1. The battle was fought between Hyder Ali of Mysore and the British East India Company led by Sir Eyre Coote.
2. The battle was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War, in which Hyder Ali played a key role before his death in 1782.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.
The Battle of Porto Novo (1781) was fought between Hyder Ali and the East India Company (EIC), led by Sir Eyre Coote. Hyder Ali was a key figure in the Anglo-Mysore Wars. The battle was part of the Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-1784). Hyder Ali died during this conflict in 1782, after which his son Tipu Sultan continued the war.

questions.question: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Battle of Plassey.
The Battle of Plassey took place in Bengal on June 23, 1757. British East India Company troops, led by Robert Clive, confronted the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, along with his French allies. The British East India Company won this battle, which is considered the formal beginning of British political dominance (Raj) in India.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764 between the British East India Company and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II.
Reason (R): After the Battle of Buxar, Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the British East India Company.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
The Battle of Buxar was fought between the British East India Company and the combined armies of Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. The British won this battle. As a result, Shah Alam II granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company, which explains the significance of the battle.

questions.question: Where was the first jute mill set up in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rishra (West Bengal, 1855).
The first jute mill (Acland Mill) was established by British entrepreneur George Acland and Bengali financier Babu By Sumber Sen in the Bengal Presidency at Rishra. In 1854, the first modern cotton mill was established in Mumbai by Cowaszee Nanabhyo Davar.

questions.question:
Statement 1: Cotton and jute industries existed in India during the British rule.
Statement 2: The iron and steel industry in India was started only after independence.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
  • Statement 1 is true: Cotton and jute industries existed in India during British rule.
  • Statement 2 is false: The first iron and steel mill was established in 1907 in Jamshedpur by Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), before independence.

questions.question: In the 18th century, the development of cotton industries in Britain resulted in
questions.option_1: Increase in demand of Indian textile in Britain
questions.option_2: Decline of textiles production in India
questions.option_3: Increase in demand of Indian textile in India
questions.option_4: Decline of British textiles industries in India
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Decline of textiles production in India.
The development of cotton industries in Britain led to the decline of textile production in India because the British Government imposed high duties on Indian textiles, making export to England difficult. The first cotton textile mill in India was established at Fort Glastor near Kolkata (1818).

questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Queen Elizabeth I.
By the Charter of 1600 A.D., the East India Company got the sole right to trade with the East, without competition from other British traders. The Company's ships first arrived in India at the port of Surat in 1608.

questions.question: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river ______ in 1651.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hugli.
The first English factory in India (temporary) was at Masulipatam (1611). The first permanent English factory was at Surat (1613). The first English factory on the banks of the river Hugli was set up in 1651.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both I and II.
The question likely refers to two statements about the East India Company army (though the specific statements are not visible in the extracted text, the solution indicates both are correct). The East India Company maintained three separate armies - Bengal, Bombay, and Madras Presidencies, with sepoys (Indian soldiers) commanded by British officers.

questions.question: The British East India Company captured Pondicherry (Puducherry) from the French in the year
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1761.
The British East India Company captured Pondicherry from the French in 1761. Pondicherry got its freedom from the French on 1st November 1954. The Union Territory of Puducherry comprises the erstwhile French colonies viz. Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.

questions.question: Which monument was built in 1924 to welcome King George V and Queen Mary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gateway of India.
The Gateway of India is an arch-monument built in the early 20th century in the city of Mumbai. It was built in 1924 to welcome King George V and Queen Mary.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE about Rash Behari Bose?
questions.option_1: He founded Indian Independence League in Tokyo in 1942.
questions.option_2: He was an important figure in the Ghadar Movement and in the formation of the Azad Hind Fauj.
questions.option_3: He was honoured with the prestigious title 'Order of the rising sun'.
questions.option_4: He was independent India's first Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is He was independent India's first Commander-in-Chief of Indian Army.
The first Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army after independence was General Sir Robert Lockhart, and the first Indian to hold the post was Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa, who took command in 1949. Rash Behari Bose was not associated with this position.

questions.question: Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Abhinash Bhattacharya and Bhupendranath Dutta were associated with which movement in March 1906?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Swadeshi movement.
In March 1906, Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Abhinash Bhattacharya, and Bhupendranath Dutta started the revolutionary Bengali weekly newspaper Jugantar. This publication served as the mouthpiece for the revolutionary organization Anushilan Samiti and was a key part of the radical nationalist stream that emerged during the Swadeshi movement, which began in 1905.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding revolts in India during British rule:
Statement 1: Tirot Sing, a Khasi chief, played a leading role in the Khasi uprising against the British from 1829 to 1833.
Statement 2: The Singpho Rebellion took place in Bengal during the late 18th century.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect.
  • Statement 1 is correct: Tirot Sing (also known as U Tirot Sing Syiem) was a Khasi chief who led the Khasi uprising (Anglo-Khasi War) from 1829 to 1833.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Singpho Rebellion of 1830 took place in Assam, not Bengal. The Sanyasi Uprisings took place in Bengal between 1770-1820s.

questions.question: The planned large-scale disruption of rail communications and the seizure of arms in Bengal were undertaken under the leadership of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jatin Mukherjee.
Jatin Mukherjee, also known as Bagha Jatin, was a prominent revolutionary leader in Bengal during the early 20th century who fought against British colonial rule. He was a key member of the Anushilan Samiti, a revolutionary organization that planned large-scale armed resistance against the British, including disruption of rail communications and seizure of arms.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chittagong Armoury Raid:
Statement 1: The Chittagong Armoury Raid was led by Surya Sen, also known as Master Da.
Statement 2: The raid took place on April 18, 1930, in present-day Bangladesh.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both statements are True.
  • Statement 1 is true: Surya Sen (also known as Master Da) led the Chittagong Armoury Raid. He founded The Indian Republican Army.
  • Statement 2 is true: The raid took place on April 18, 1930, in Chittagong (now in Bangladesh).

questions.question: Sido and Kanhu were leaders of which of the following tribal rebellions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Santhal Rebellion.
The Santhal Rebellion (Hul revolt) began in 1855, led by Sidhu, Kanhu, Chand, Bhairav, and their sisters Phulo and Jhano.

questions.question: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1911.
Vinayak Damodar Savarkar was sent to the Cellular Jail (Kala Pani) in Andaman in 1911 under the Nashik Conspiracy Case for the murder of the Collector of Nashik District, Jackson. While serving his sentence, he wrote the epic 'Kamala' on the prison walls.

questions.question: In 1910, The United India House at Seattle, USA, was set up by
questions.option_2: Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tarak Nath Das and GD Kumar.
They were Indian revolutionaries who collaborated to promote Indian independence from British rule. Shyamji Krishna Varma founded the Indian Home Rule Society, India House, and The Indian Sociologist in London. Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar established the Abhinav Bharat Society in 1904.

questions.question: Which of the following groups/parties was started in San Francisco, United States of America during the Indian National Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ghadar Party.
The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in the U.S. as the Hindi Association of the Pacific Coast. It aimed to free India from British rule. It was founded by Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Har Dayal in San Francisco.

questions.question: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote a novel Anand Math based on which of the following rebellions/revolts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sanyasi Rebellion.
The Sanyasi Uprisings took place in Bengal between 1770-1820s. The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram', is an excerpt taken from the novel Anand Math written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, which was based on the Sanyasi Rebellion.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Bombay Presidency Association (1885):
Statement 1: The Bombay Presidency Association was founded in 1885 by Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, and K.T. Telang.
Statement 2: Zakir Husain was one of the founders of the Bombay Presidency Association.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False.
  • Statement 1 is true: The Bombay Presidency Association was founded in 1885 by Badruddin Tyabji, Pherozeshah Mehta, and K.T. Telang.
  • Statement 2 is false: Zakir Husain was not a founder of the Bombay Presidency Association. Badruddin Tyabji was the third President (1887) of INC and the first Muslim to hold that position.

questions.question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Khilafat Movement.
The Khilafat Movement was a political campaign from 1919 to 1922 in British India. It was a protest against the British government's policies towards Turkey and the planned dismantling of the Ottoman Empire after World War I.

questions.question: Who was executed as an accomplice to the murder of AMT Jackson?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Krishnaji Gopal Karve.
The Jackson murder case, also known as the Nasik Conspiracy (Year 1909), involved Anant Laxman Kanhere shooting Jackson, the Collector of Nashik. Krishnaji Gopal Karve was executed as an accomplice. The event led to the arrest of Savarkar.

questions.question: Which of the following revolutionists was associated with the Anushilan Samiti?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Jatindra Mohan Sengupta.
Anushilan Samiti was founded by Satish Chandra Bose and Barrister Praanath Mitra. Jatindra Mohan Sengupta was associated with it. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were members of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
